Busselton, WA

Shipping containers Busselton

Busselton sits on low, flat land between the calm water of Geographe Bay and the Vasse wetlands, and the country changes character as you head west. Dunsborough, Eagle Bay and Yallingup climb onto the granite and limestone of the cape, then Caves Road runs south through vineyards and forest to Margaret River. Container work down here is a mix no other part of the state quite matches: winery sheds, holiday houses whose owners live in Perth, new estates at Vasse and Yalyalup, surf and boat gear, and cattle and dairy country behind the coast. Each needs a slightly different conversation.

The jobs they turn up on locally

Around Busselton we deliver containers for barrel, bin and equipment storage at the wineries and vineyards from Yallingup down through Wilyabrup and Cowaramup to Margaret River, linen and maintenance gear for holiday rental managers, boats, kayaks and surfboards for households in Dunsborough, Quindalup and Eagle Bay, site stores on the estates growing through Vasse, Yalyalup and Dunsborough Lakes, staging and equipment for events between seasons, hay, fencing and machinery on the beef and dairy country inland toward Carbunup and Metricup, and stock and packaging for the breweries and distilleries along Caves Road.

Getting a truck in

Town and cape are two different delivery landscapes. Busselton itself is flat, with generous streets and older lots in West Busselton, Broadwater and Abbey that usually have space down one side. The newer estates at Vasse, Yalyalup and Provence are laid out for cars and trailers and are generally easy for a tilt-tray. The cape is harder. Around Dunsborough, Eagle Bay and Yallingup, many lots are steep, rocky and heavily treed with peppermint, marri and banksia, and the roads are narrow with little shoulder. Driveways can drop sharply off the road or bend between granite boulders, and a container that can be placed on a flat site in town may need a crane on the cape. Caves Road is the main artery south and it is busy. During school holidays, around Christmas and at Easter it fills with caravans, cyclists and visitors looking at the view instead of the road, so deliveries are best booked outside the peak. Wineries and farms have their own rhythm: gravel tracks, vineyard rows, fruit bins stacked in the yard, and gates that need to be left as found. Around Margaret River the forest closes in, especially through the tall karri stands to the south, and overhanging branches decide how high a load can travel. Whatever the address, a photo from the road, one along the drive and one of the spot usually answers every question before a truck leaves Fremantle.

Busselton

Low ground between the bay and the Vasse

Much of Busselton sits only a few metres above sea level, with the Vasse River, the Lower Vasse and the Vasse-Wonnerup wetlands at its back and the bay at its front. In summer that makes very little difference. Through a wet winter the water table comes up under the sandy ground, low corners of lots stay wet for weeks, and the lawn that looked firm in February will not take a loaded truck in August. If your block is near the wetlands or in one of the lower streets, tell us where the water sits after rain, because that is where the truck should not go and where the container should not be placed.

The setup that suits this ground is pads or sleepers under each corner, levelled against one another and set on the firmest part of the lot, with the floor kept clear of the sand so it can dry out. On the lowest land it is worth thinking about storms as well. When a winter front pushes water into the bay on a big tide, the lowest parts of town can see water where it is not usually found. A container keeps rain off from above but it does nothing to keep rising water out. Seawater pushed up through the town will find its way around door gaskets, and a light, empty unit can be floated clear of where you left it. Put it on the high side of the block and keep anything that matters up off the floor.

Inland, the beef and dairy country toward Carbunup, Metricup and Jindong tells the same story on a larger scale. Paddocks that carry a truck easily through summer turn heavy and wet after the winter rains, and gateways churned by stock and tractors are the softest ground on the farm. Farm drops are best planned for when the ground is dry, or onto a gravel pad near the sheds where a loader can move the container later. Tell us the width of the gateway at its narrowest point, whether there is a grid or culvert on the way in, and where a loaded truck can turn around.

On the ground

Wineries, vintage and what a steel box does to wine

Wineries and vineyards through Wilyabrup, Yallingup and Margaret River use containers for barrels, dry goods, packaging, irrigation parts, tractors and spare equipment. The one thing to plan around is vintage, which usually runs late summer into autumn. For those weeks every road into a vineyard is full of harvesters, bin trailers and trucks carrying fruit, and nobody has spare time to meet a container delivery. Get it in before vintage starts, or after the last fruit is in, and make sure the drop point will not be in the way of the fruit coming in.

Temperature is the other issue for anyone storing wine or anything temperature sensitive. A standard steel container in full sun gets hot inside on a summer afternoon, and it swings more than a well-insulated building would. That is fine for tanks, hoses, tools and packaging. It is not fine for bottled stock or barrels holding wine. For those, ask about an insulated or refrigerated unit, or at least site the container in shade with good ventilation. A light roof colour helps a little. Tell us what is going in and we will match the container to it rather than leave you to find out in February.

Worth knowing

Holiday houses and owners who live somewhere else

A lot of homes on the cape are holiday houses and rentals whose owners live in Perth or further away. Those deliveries work smoothly when the details are settled in advance, and go wrong when the driver arrives at a locked gate with nobody answering the phone. We need a contact who can answer on the day, the gate code or key arrangement, a note on whether any dogs are on the property, and a photo of the exact spot with something in the picture that marks the corner. If a property manager looks after the house, put us in touch with them. If a neighbour will be there, that works too.

It is also worth checking what the local rules allow before a container lands on a holiday lot. The City of Busselton covers Busselton, Dunsborough and Yallingup, while Margaret River, Cowaramup and Augusta fall under the Shire of Augusta-Margaret River. Each has its own view on containers in residential and rural areas, and strata or estate rules can add more. A short call before ordering avoids a letter later. Call 1300 467 776 with the holiday address and what you need stored; the quote you receive covers both the box and the trip down from Fremantle.

Holiday rentals have their own uses for a container. Managers use them to hold spare linen, outdoor furniture, cleaning gear and the barbecue that has to vanish before guests arrive, while owners use them to lock away the boat, the surfboards and the car trailer when the house is let out. A lockable box separate from the house means a family's belongings stay out of reach of guests without a room being shut off. Site it where guests will not reverse into it, and where it will not spoil the view that someone is paying to look at.

Common questions

Buying a container in Busselton

Can you deliver to a winery during vintage?

We can, but it is rarely the best plan. During vintage every vineyard track is busy with harvesters, bin trailers and fruit trucks, and a container delivery gets in the way. Booking before vintage starts or after the last fruit is in makes everyone's life easier. If it must happen mid-vintage, give us a contact who can direct the driver and a drop point well clear of where the fruit comes in.

Can you deliver to my Dunsborough holiday house while I am in Perth?

Yes. We need someone we can reach on the day, the gate code or key arrangements, whether there are dogs on the property, and a photo of the exact spot with something that marks it clearly. A property manager or a neighbour on site makes it easier still. If the block is steep or heavily treed, send a photo along the driveway as well so we can decide between a tilt-tray and a crane truck.

Is Margaret River covered by the City of Busselton?

No. Busselton, Dunsborough, Yallingup and Vasse are in the City of Busselton, while Margaret River, Cowaramup, Witchcliffe and Augusta are in the Shire of Augusta-Margaret River. Each has its own rules on containers in residential and rural zones, so check with the right one for your address before you order. We deliver to both.

Can I store wine in a shipping container?

Not in a standard one left in the sun. A plain steel container heats up quickly on a summer afternoon and cools overnight, and that swing is hard on bottled wine and barrels. For wine, ask about an insulated or refrigerated container. For tools, tanks, packaging and machinery a standard unit is fine, especially if it is shaded and ventilated. Tell us what is going in when you enquire.

Can a container go on a steep block at Eagle Bay or Yallingup?

Often, yes, but it usually needs a crane truck rather than a tilt-tray. Cape blocks tend to fall away from the road with granite, peppermints and banksia in the way, and a tilt-tray needs a straight, firm run to the spot. A crane truck can reach over from the road if there is clear air above the lot. Send photos of the road, the drive and the spot, and mention any overhead power so we can tell you what will work.
